verses.text: Den Job answer say,
“Listen well to my speech. Make dis be your comfort.
Allow me, make I talk too, and after I don talk, una fit mock.
As for me, my complaint na to man? Why I no go lose patience?
Look me, and shock. Put your hand for your mouth.
When I remember, I dey troubled. Fear dey hold my flesh.
Why di wicked dey live, grow old, yes, and grow strong for power?
Dem pikin dey stand with dem before dem eyes, dem children before dem eyes.
Dem houses dey safe from fear, and God rod no dey on dem.
Dem bull dey breed without fail. Dem cow dey born calf and no dey miscarry.
Dem dey send out dem small pikin like flock. Dem children dey dance.
Dem dey sing with drum and harp and dey rejoice for di sound of flute.
Dem dey spend dem days for wealth. For one moment dem go down to Sheol.
Dem dey talk to God say, ‘Leave us, because we no wan know your ways.
Wetin be di Almighty, say we go serve am? Wetin we go gain if we pray to am?’
Look, dem good fortune no dey dem hand. Di advice of di wicked far from me.
How many times dem don put out di lamp of di wicked, how many times dem disaster don come on dem, how many times God don share sorrow for im anger?
How many times dem don be like dry grass before wind, like chaff wey storm carry go?
Una talk say, ‘God dey keep im wrong for im pikin dem.’ Make e pay am to imself, so dat e go know am.
Make im own eyes see im destruction. Make e drink from di anger of di Almighty.
Because wetin e go enjoy for im house after am, when di number of im months don cut off?
Anybody go teach God knowledge, since e dey judge dem wey dey high?
One person die for im full strength, completely at ease and quiet.
Im buckets full of milk. Di marrow of im bones dey wet.
Another one die with bitter soul, wey never eat with joy.
Dem lie down together for dust, and worm cover dem.
Look, I know una thoughts, di plans wey una wan use do me wrong.
Because una talk say, ‘Where di prince house dey? Where di tent dey wey di wicked live?’
Una no ask people wey dey travel? Una no know dem signs,
say di evil man dey kept for di day of disaster, say dem dey carry dem go for di day of anger?
Who go tell am im way to im face? Who go pay am back wetin e don do?
Still dem go carry am go di grave. People go keep watch over im tomb.
Di dirt of di valley go sweet am. Everybody go follow am, as plenty don go before am.
So how una take dey comfort me with nonsense, since for una answers only lie remain?”
Den Eliphaz di Temanite answer say,
“Man fit profit God? Sure sure di wise man dey profit imself.
E dey please di Almighty say you dey righteous? Or e dey gain am say you dey make your ways perfect?
Na because of your fear of God e dey correct you, say e dey enter judgment with you?
No be say your wickedness big? And your wrongs no get end.
Because you don take pledges from your brother for nothing and strip di naked of dem clothes.
You no give water to di tired to drink. You hold back bread from di hungry.
But di mighty man get di earth, and di honored man dey stay inside am.
You don send widows away empty. Dem don break di arms of di orphans.
So traps dey round you. Sudden fear dey trouble you,
or darkness, so dat you no fit see, and floods of water dey cover you.
No be say God dey di height of heaven? Look di height of di stars, how high dem dey!
You talk say, ‘Wetin God know? E fit judge through thick darkness?
Thick clouds cover am so dat e no see. E dey waka for di circle of heaven.’
You go keep di old way wey wicked men don waka,
wey dem snatch go before dem time, wey dem foundation pour out like stream,
wey talk to God say, ‘Leave us,’ and, ‘Wetin di Almighty fit do for us?’
Yet e fill dem houses with good things, but di advice of di wicked far from me.
Di righteous see am and dey glad. Di innocent dey laugh at dem,
dey talk say, ‘Sure sure dem wey rise against us don cut off. Fire don burn dem remain.’
Now know am well and dey peace. Through dat good go come to you.
I beg you, receive teaching from im mouth. Keep im words for your heart.
If you return to di Almighty, e go build you up, if you put wickedness far from your tents.
Put your treasure for dust, di gold of Ophir among di stones of di streams.
Di Almighty go be your treasure and precious silver to you.
Because den you go enjoy di Almighty and lift your face to God.
You go pray to am, and e go hear you. You go pay your promises.
You go decide one thing too, and e go stand for you. Light go shine on your ways.
When dem throw you down, you go talk say, ‘Lift up!’ E go save di humble person.
E go even save di innocent. Yes, dem go save am through di cleanness of your hands.”
Den Job answer say,
“Even today my complaint na rebellion. Im hand heavy even as I dey groan.
Oh, if I know where I fit find am! Make I come reach im seat!
I for arrange my case before am and fill my mouth with arguments.
I for know di words wey e go answer me and understand wetin e go tell me.
E go argue with me with di greatness of im power? No, but e go listen to me.
Dere di honest fit argue with am, so I go free forever from my judge.
Look, I dey go forward, but e no dey dere. I dey go back, but I no fit see am.
For di left side, when e dey work, but I no fit see am. E dey hide for di right side, so I no fit see am.
But e know di way wey I dey take. When e don test me, I go come out like gold.
My foot don hold im steps tight. I don keep im way and no turn aside.
I no go back from di command of im lips. I don keep di words of im mouth pass my daily food.
But e dey stand alone, and who fit oppose am? Wetin im soul want, na dat e dey do.
Because e dey finish wetin e don appoint for me. Plenty dis kind things dey with am.
So I dey fear before am. When I think, I dey fear am.
Because God don make my heart faint. Di Almighty don frighten me.
Because dem no cut me off before di darkness, and e no cover di thick darkness from my face.”
“Why di Almighty no keep times for imself? Why dem wey know am no see im days?
Some dey remove boundary marks. Dem dey take flocks by force and dey feed on dem.
Dem dey drive away di orphan donkey. Dem dey take di widow ox as pledge.
Dem dey push di needy out of di way. Di poor of di earth dey hide dem self.
Look, like wild donkeys for desert dem dey go out to dem work, dey look for food well well. Di wilderness dey give dem bread for dem pikin dem.
Dem dey cut dem food for di field. Dem dey pick di vineyard harvest of di wicked.
Dem dey lie down for night naked without clothes and no get cover for cold.
Di rain of di mountains dey wet dem, and dem dey hold di rock because dem no get shelter.
Some dey snatch di orphan from di breast and dey take pledge from di poor,
so dat dem dey waka naked without clothes, and as dem dey hungry dem dey carry di bundles of grain.
Dem dey make oil inside di walls of dis men. Dem dey press dem grapes and dey suffer thirst.
From di city wey full of people, men dey groan. Di soul of di wounded dey cry out. Still God no dey look di foolishness.
Dem na among dem wey rebel against di light. Dem no know im ways and no dey stay for im paths.
Di murderer dey rise with di light. E dey kill di poor and needy. For night e be like thief.
Di eye of di adulterer dey wait for evening, dey talk say, ‘No eye go see me.’ E dey cover im face.
For dark dem dey break into houses. For daytime dem dey lock dem self inside. Dem no know light.
Because for all of dem, morning na like di shadow of death. Because dem know di terrors of di shadow of death.
Una talk say, ‘Dem dey fast for di face of di waters. Dem share dey cursed for di earth. Dem no dey turn go di way of di vineyards.’
Drought and heat dey finish snow water, so Sheol dey do to dem wey don sin.
Di womb go forget am. Worm go feed sweet on am. Dem no go remember am again. Wickedness go break like tree.
E dey eat di barren woman wey no dey born. E no dey do good to di widow.
Yet God dey keep di mighty by im power. E dey rise wey no get assurance of life.
God dey give dem security, and dem dey rest for am. Im eyes dey on dem ways.
Dem dey lifted up, but for small time and dem don go. Yes, dem dey brought low, dem dey remove dem from di way like all others, and dem dey cut off like di tops of di ears of grain.
If e no be so now, who go show say I be liar and make my speech turn to nothing?”
Den Bildad di Shuhite answer say,
“Power and fear dey with am. E dey make peace for im high places.
Number dey for im armies? On who im light no dey rise?
So how man fit dey righteous before God? Or how di one wey woman born fit be clean?
Look, even di moon no get brightness, and di stars no pure for im sight,
how much less man, wey be worm, di son of man, wey be worm!”
Den Job answer say,
“How you don help am wey no get power! How you don save di arm wey no get strength!
How you don advise am wey no get wisdom and plenty declare good knowledge!
To who you don talk dis words? Whose spirit come out from you?
Di dead spirits dey tremble under di waters and all wey dey live inside dem.
Sheol dey naked before am. Abaddon no get cover.
E dey stretch out di north over empty space and dey hang di earth for nothing.
E dey tie up di waters for im thick clouds, and di cloud no dey burst under dem.
E dey cover di face of im throne and spread im cloud on am.
E don draw boundary on di face of di waters, to di edge of light and darkness.
Di pillars of heaven dey tremble and dey shock at im warning.
E dey stir up di sea with im power, and with im understanding e dey strike Rahab.
By im Spirit di heavens dey beautiful. Im hand don pierce di fast snake.
Look, dis na only di edge of im ways. How small whisper we dey hear about am! But di thunder of im power, who fit understand?”
Job take im parable again and talk say,
“As God dey live, wey don take away my right, di Almighty, wey don make my soul bitter,
because my life still dey full inside me and God breath dey my nose,
sure sure my lips no go talk wickedness and my tongue no go talk deceit.
E far from me say I go say una dey right. Until I die I no go remove my honesty from me.
I hold my righteousness tight and I no go let am go. My heart no go blame me as long as I dey live.
Make my enemy be like di wicked, di one wey rise against me like di unrighteous.
Because wetin be di hope of di godless, when dem cut am off, when God take away im life?
God go hear im cry when trouble come on am?
E go enjoy di Almighty and call on God every time?
I go teach una about God hand. Wetin dey with di Almighty I no go hide.
Look, una all don see am una self. So why una don turn completely empty?
Dis na di share of wicked man with God, di inheritance of oppressors wey dem receive from di Almighty.
If im pikin dem plenty, na for sword. Im children no go satisfy with bread.
Dem wey remain of am go bury for death. Im widows no go cry.
Even if e gather silver like dust and prepare clothes like clay,
e fit prepare am, but di righteous go wear am, and di innocent go share di silver.
E dey build im house like moth, like hut wey watchman dey make.
E dey lie down rich, but dem no go gather am. E open im eyes, and e no dey again.
Terrors dey catch am like water. Storm dey carry am go for night.
East wind dey carry am go, and e dey go. E sweep am from im place.
Because e dey throw am and no dey spare, e dey run quick from im hand.
Men go clap dem hands at am and whistle am out of im place.”
“Sure sure place dey for silver, and place dey for gold wey dem dey refine.
Dem dey take iron from di earth, and dem dey melt copper from di stone.
Man dey put end to darkness and dey search to di farthest edge for di stones of darkness and thick darkness.
E dey break open hole far from where people dey stay. Dem dey forget dem for foot. Dem dey hang far from men and dey swing go and come.
As for di earth, bread dey come out from am. Underneath, dem dey turn am like fire.
Im stones na di place of sapphires, and e get gold dust.
Dat path no bird of prey know, and di falcon eye no see am.
Di proud animals no waka am, and di fierce lion no pass am.
E put im hand on di hard rock. E dey overturn di mountains from dem roots.
E dey cut channels among di rocks. Im eye dey see every precious thing.
E dey tie di streams so dat dem no drip. Wetin hidden, e dey bring am out to light.
But where dem go find wisdom? Where di place of understanding dey?
Man no know im price, and dem no find am for di land of di living.
Di deep talk say, ‘E no dey inside me.’ Di sea talk say, ‘E no dey with me.’
Dem no fit buy am with gold, and dem no go weigh silver as im price.
Dem no fit value am with di gold of Ophir, with di precious onyx or di sapphire.
Gold and glass no fit equal am, and dem no go exchange am for fine gold jewels.
Dem no go mention coral or crystal. Yes, di price of wisdom pass rubies.
Di topaz of Ethiopia no go equal am, and dem no go value am with pure gold.
So where wisdom dey come from? Where di place of understanding dey?
Since e dey hidden from di eyes of all living things and dey kept from di birds of di sky.
Destruction and Death talk say, ‘We don hear rumor about am with our ears.’
God understand im way, and e know im place.
Because e dey look reach di ends of di earth and dey see under all di sky.
E dey set di force of di wind. Yes, e dey measure di waters.
When e make law for di rain and way for di lightning of di thunder,
den e see am and declare am. E set am up, yes, and search am out.
To man e talk say, ‘Look, di fear of di Lord, na wisdom. To turn away from evil na understanding.’”
Job take im parable again and talk say,
“Oh, if I dey like di months of old, like di days when God dey watch over me,
when im lamp dey shine on my head, and by im light I dey waka through darkness,
as I dey for di ripeness of my days, when God friendship dey on my tent,
when di Almighty still dey with me and my pikin dem dey round me,
when my steps dey wash with butter and di rock dey pour out streams of oil for me!
When I go out to di gate of di city, when I prepare my seat for di street,
di young men see me and hide. Di old men stand up.
Di princes stop to talk and put dem hand for dem mouth.
Di voice of di nobles quiet, and dem tongue stick to di roof of dem mouth.
Because when di ear hear me, e bless me, and when di eye see me, e praise me,
because I save di poor wey dey cry and di orphan wey no get helper.
Di blessing of am wey dey ready to perish come on me. I make di widow heart sing for joy.
I wear righteousness, and e cover me. My justice be like robe and crown.
I be eyes to di blind and feet to di lame.
I be papa to di needy. I search out di case of am wey I no know.
I break di jaws of di wicked and pull di prey from im teeth.
Den I talk say, ‘I go die for my nest. I go increase my days like sand.
My root dey spread to di waters. Dew dey lie for my branch all night.
My glory dey fresh inside me. My bow dey new for my hand.’
People dey listen to me, dey wait and dey keep quiet for my advice.
After my words dem no dey talk again. My speech dey drop on dem.
Dem dey wait for me like rain. Dem dey open dem mouth wide like for spring rain.
I dey smile for dem when dem no get confidence. Dem no reject di light of my face.
I choose out dem way and sit as chief. I dey live like king among di army, like person wey dey comfort mourners.”
“But now dem wey young pass me dey laugh at me, dem papa dem wey I no gree put with di dogs of my flock.
Indeed, wetin di strength of dem hands go profit me? Dem strength don perish.
Dem dey thin from hunger and famine. Dem dey chew di dry ground for di gloom of waste and desolation.
Dem dey pluck salty plants by di bushes. Di roots of broom na dem food.
Dem dey drive dem out from among men. People dey shout after dem like thief,
so dat dem dey stay for frightening valleys, for holes of di earth and of di rocks.
Among di bushes dem dey cry like donkey. Under di nettles dem dey squeeze together.
Dem na pikin of fools, yes, pikin of vile men. Dem whip dem out of di land.
Now I don become dem song. Yes, I be proverb to dem.
Dem hate me, dem stand far from me and no dey hold spit back from my face.
Because e don loosen im rope and afflict me, and dem don throw off restraint before me.
For my right hand di rabble dey rise. Dem dey push my feet aside, and dem dey build against me dem ways of destruction.
Dem dey spoil my path. Dem dey push my destruction without anybody help.
Dem dey come like through wide hole for wall. Dem dey roll enter inside di ruin.
Terrors don turn on me. Dem dey chase my honor like wind. My good fortune don pass like cloud.
Now my soul pour out inside me. Days of suffering don hold me.
For night my bones dey pierce inside me, and di pains wey dey gnaw me no dey rest.
By big force my cloth don spoil. E dey tie me round like di collar of my coat.
E don throw me inside mud. I don turn like dust and ashes.
I cry to you, and you no answer me. I stand up, and you dey look me.
You don turn cruel to me. With di strength of your hand you dey chase me.
You lift me up to di wind and drive me with am. You dey dissolve me for di storm.
Because I know say you go bring me to death, to di house wey dem don appoint for all living.
But person no dey stretch out hand when e dey fall? Or for im disaster e no dey cry for help?
I no cry for am wey dey trouble? My soul no grieve for di needy?
When I look for good, den evil come. When I wait for light, darkness come.
My heart dey troubled and no dey rest. Days of suffering don come on me.
I dey waka dey mourn without sun. I stand up for di gathering and cry for help.
I be brother to jackals and friend to ostriches.
My skin dey turn black and dey fall from me. My bones dey burn with heat.
So my harp don turn to mourning and my flute to di voice of dem wey dey cry.”
